If $b<\infty$ and there are $b_0\in(a,b)$ and a compact set $K\subset\mathcal D$ such that $z([b_0,b))\subseteq K$, then the solution extends beyond $b$, contradicting maximality. actual_use_anchors: Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ with $a<b$. A configuration on $[a,b]$ consists of a $C^2$ curve $x:[a,b]\to M$ and a smooth positive function $e:[a,b]\to(0,\infty)$ on the prescribed background of [[post-rpm-test-clock-and-background]]. Vary $x$ and $e$ independently: $x$ through $C^2$ variations $H:(-\epsilon_0,\epsilon_0)\times[a,b]\to M$ for some $\epsilon_0>0$, with $H(0,s)=x(s)$ and $H(\epsilon,a)=x(a)$, $H(\epsilon,b)=x(b)$, and no causal restriction on the varied curves; and $e$ through jointly smooth positive variations $e_\epsilon:[a,b]\to(0,\infty)$ whose variation field $\delta e:=\partial_\epsilon e_\epsilon|_{\epsilon=0}$ is compactly supported in $(a,b)$. Adopt a distinct massless test-particle sector with primitive action

and stationary under all such independent variations. The variational equations and their null branch follow from [[lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalence]]: the constraint is $g(T,T)=0$, and the physical branch requires $T$ to be nonzero and future-directed. The associated momentum $P=T/e$ is nonzero future null; its positive scale is primitive initial data, not $mU$ for any $m=0$ substitution. Null curves have no proper-time parameter. With $s$ in seconds, $T$ in metres per second, and $e$ in kg$^{-1}$, the integral has units joule-seconds. For finite intervals $[a',b']$ and $[a,b]$, an orientation-preserving $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $s=\phi(r):[a',b']\to[a,b]$ with $\phi'>0$ transforms $T_r(r)=\phi'(r)T(\phi(r))$ and $e_r(r)=\phi'(r)e(\phi(r))$; this leaves the functional invariant by [[lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalence]] and preserves the stated configuration class. Neither the scale nor a clock reading is inferred from the ray image alone.

actual_use_anchors: On a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian background, stationarity for the massive action of [[post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action]] is defined on a finite segment $[a,b]$ with the stated fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations. A stationary massive path on that segment satisfies $D_\tau U=0$ in proper-time parameter, with $P=mU$ and $m>0$ constant. In the separately adopted null sector of [[post-rpm-null-test-particle-action]], stationarity for the einbein action is likewise defined on a finite segment, using independent fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations of the curve and smooth interior variations of the einbein. Its nonzero future-null branch has momentum $P$ satisfying $D_\lambda P=0$ in an affine parameter $\lambda$ with $dx/d\lambda=P$. These equations hold locally on the interiors of the finite segments; their ODE solutions extend uniquely to maximal solutions on open intervals, with no action integrated over an infinite interval. For any $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$ and $p_0\in M$, an initial vector $U_0\in T_{p_0}M$ that is future timelike and satisfies $g_{p_0}(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$ determines a unique local massive solution with $x(\tau_0)=p_0$, $U(\tau_0)=U_0$, and a unique maximal solution on an open interval containing $\tau_0$. For any $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$ and $p_0\in M$, a nonzero future-null vector $P_0\in T_{p_0}M$ determines a unique local null solution with $x(\lambda_0)=p_0$, $P(\lambda_0)=P_0$, and a unique maximal solution on an open interval containing $\lambda_0$. Neither maximal interval is asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

[F1] On each finite segment $[a,b]$, the adopted massive action is $-mc\int_a^b\ell ds$ and its variations are fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations ([[post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action]]); the mechanical momentum is $P=mU$ ([[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]), and stationarity is equivalent to $D_s(T/\ell)=0$ ([[lem-rpm-length-action-first-variation]]). The proper-time theorem gives $U=cT/\ell$ ([[thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization]]).

[F2] On each finite segment $[a,b]$, the null einbein action uses independent fixed-endpoint $C^2$ curve variations and smooth interior einbein variations; its nonzero future-null branch has $P=T/e$ and $D_\lambda P=0$ after $d\lambda=e\,ds$ ([[post-rpm-null-test-particle-action]], [[lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalence]]).

actual_use_anchors: Let $(M,g,N)$ be a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold and let $m,c>0$. Let $\mathcal V\subset TM$ be an open set of future timelike vectors, and let $f$ be a smooth vector field along the bundle projection $\mathcal V\to M$, with $f(p,V)\in T_pM$. For the named massive test body, adopt the constant-mass force model of [[post-rpm-prescribed-force-law]]: $P=mU$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, $D_\tau P=f(x,U)$, and $g(U,f(x,U))=0$. If $\tau$ is measured in seconds, then $P$ has SI units kilogram metres per second and $f$ has units newtons.

[A1] The physical model is an optional adoption for a named massive test body with constant primitive $m>0$: on an open neighborhood of the future unit timelike shell it specifies a smooth force $f$, the equation $D_\tau P=f(x,U)$ with $P=mU$, and the compatibility condition $g(U,f(x,U))=0$ ([[post-rpm-prescribed-force-law]]). This is not a universal force principle; that postulate is a current in-run draft and is used here at its inspected statement.

[L1] For a smooth force on an open future-timelike velocity domain with $g(U,f)=0$, the system $D_sx=U$, $D_sU=f(x,U)/m$ has a unique local solution, preserves $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and future direction, and has a unique maximal open interval ([[lem-rpm-shell-tangent-force-ivp]]). The actual supplier is a draft from in-run batch 22, so the use here is conditional on its inspected interface and proof status.
